title.zh: 中医养发：让头发浓密光泽的秘密
title.en: TCM Hair Care: Secrets for Thick, Glossy Hair

description.zh: 掌握中医养发的方法，从调理肝肾入手，让头发浓密光泽，告别脱发烦恼
description.en: Master TCM hair care methods, regulate liver-kidney for thick, glossy hair

zh.text: 头发向来被视为人体气血盛衰的外在标志。《黄帝内经》中有两段论述奠定了中医养发学的理论根基：其一曰"肾藏精，其华在发"，其二曰"肝藏血，发为血之余"。这两句话揭示了一个核心规律——头发的生长状态、色泽、疏密，本质上反映的是肝肾精血的充盈程度。我在临床上见到太多的脱发患者，拿着各种昂贵的生发产品来就诊，却很少有人意识到，头发的问题是身体内部失衡的"报警信号"，不从根源调理，仅靠外部涂抹，终究难以获得理想效果。
中医对头发的认识

中医认为，毛发的生长有赖于精血的濡养。《诸病源候论》云："足少阴肾之经也，其华在发。冲任之脉，为十二经之海，谓之血海……若血气盛则荣于头发，故头发美；若血气衰弱，经脉虚竭，不能荣润，故头发秃落。"这一论述精辟地阐明了头发荣枯与气血盛衰之间的必然联系。具体而言，肾精的盛衰直接影响头发的密度和色泽——肾精充足则头发浓密乌黑，肾精亏耗则头发稀疏早白。肝血的盈亏则影响头发的润泽程度——肝血上荣则发丝柔润，肝血亏虚则发质枯槁。
肾与头发

《素问·上古天真论》以肾气的盛衰描述人体生长壮老已的全过程，其中明确指出："女子三十五岁阳明脉衰，面始焦，发始堕……男子五八肾气衰，发堕齿槁。"肾精充足的人，头发自然浓密光泽；肾精不足则头发干枯、脱落、变白。我经常打一个比方：肾精就像是头发的"银行储蓄"，年轻时如果肆意挥霍——长期熬夜、过度劳累、纵欲过度，等不到老年，头发就会提前"透支"。临床上我遇到的二三十岁就开始严重脱发、大量白发的患者，几乎无一例外地有着长期熬夜和高压工作的生活史。
肝与头发
《灵枢·经脉》说："肝足厥阴之脉……上出额，与督脉会于巅。"肝藏血而厥阴经上达巅顶，肝血充足则经脉充养，发根得固、发丝得润。肝血不足时，发根失养，轻则干枯分叉，重则脱落稀疏。此外，肝主疏泄，肝气郁结也会影响头发的健康——气滞则血瘀，头皮气血供应不足，毛囊自然难以维持正常的生长周期。我在女性患者的脱发调理中尤其注重疏肝解郁，因为肝郁气滞在女性脱发的病因中占据了相当大的比重。
头发问题的原因
脱发原因

脱发的原因在中医看来可以归纳为四种主要的病理状态。其一为肾精亏虚——或先天禀赋不足，或后天损耗过度（如熬夜、过劳、房事不节），肾精不足以养发。其二为气血不足——脾为气血生化之源，饮食不节或脾胃虚弱导致气血生成不足，发失所养。其三为肝郁气滞——情绪压力过大，肝气郁结，气血运行不畅，头皮供血不足。其四为湿热上蒸——嗜食肥甘厚味，湿热内生，循经上蒸于头皮，表现为头皮油腻、毛囊堵塞、脂溢性脱发。这四种病因有时单独出现，更多时候是相互交织。我在临证中必须仔细辨明主次，才能制定有效的治疗方案。
白发原因

白发的出现同样与肝肾密切相关。肾精不足是早生白发的根本原因，《素问·上古天真论》指出肾气衰则"发鬓颁白"。气血亏虚也是常见原因——发为血之余，气血不足则头发失去色素沉着能力。情志失调同样不容忽视，我在临床上观察到，长期焦虑、压力巨大的人群中，白发往往出现得更早、进展更快。此外，遗传禀赋也是重要影响因素，有些人天生肾精偏弱，三十出头便见白发，这属于先天因素，虽然无法逆转，但通过后天调理完全可以延缓进展。
养发方法
补肾养发

补肾是养发的第一要务，黑色食材是补肾的代表。黑芝麻色黑入肾，《本草备要》称其"补肝肾、润五脏、填精髓"，且富含油脂，对发丝有天然的滋润作用。核桃形似人脑，以形补形，补肾健脑的同时亦能养发乌发。何首乌在《本草纲目》中被誉为"滋补良药"，"能养血益肝，固精益肾，健筋骨，乌髭发"，是中医养发最著名的药材之一，但需注意生何首乌有肝毒性，须经炮制后方可使用，且不宜长期大量服用。枸杞滋补肝肾、益精明目，每日嚼服或泡水都有很好的养发效果。黑豆补肾益精，《本草纲目拾遗》记载其"明目、益发"，可煮粥或磨豆浆。
养血养发

养血是养发的另一重要支柱。当归被《本草纲目》称为"血中圣药"，既能补血又能活血，使新血得生、旧血得行，是养血养发的首选药物。熟地经过九蒸九晒炮制后，药性由凉转温，补血滋阴之力更甚，常与当归同用。阿胶为驴皮熬制而成，补血滋阴、润燥止血，《本草纲目》称其"和血滋阴，除风润燥"，对于血虚所致的发枯、脱发有很好的改善作用。红枣补气养血，虽作用温和，但适合长期作为日常食疗。我在临床上常将当归、熟地、红枣配伍，辅以黄芪补气以生血，制成茶饮或煲汤，适合气血两虚型脱发患者长期调理。
养发穴位

头部穴位按摩是养发的重要手段。百会穴位于头顶正中，是诸阳之会，按揉可提升阳气、促进头部气血运行、刺激毛囊活性。肾俞穴位于腰部第二腰椎棘突下旁开1.5寸，虽不在头部，但通过补肾而养发，是"上病下取"的体现。太溪穴位于内踝后方与跟腱之间的凹陷处，是肾经原穴，按揉可补肾益精。三阴交位于小腿内侧、内踝尖上3寸，是肝脾肾三经交会穴，调补气血效果显著。风池穴在后颈部，按揉可改善头部供血。我建议患者每日用梳子或指腹从前额向后颈方向梳理按摩头皮5至10分钟，重点刺激上述穴位，长期坚持对改善发质和减少脱发有明确帮助。
头皮按摩方法

头皮按摩是养发中最简单易行的方法。具体做法是：用十指指腹从前额发际线开始，沿头皮向后颈方向做螺旋状按揉，力度适中，以头皮感到微微发热为佳。然后用木质或牛角梳子从前额向后颈缓慢梳理，每次50至100下，可有效促进头皮血液循环。百会穴和风池穴可用拇指或食指重点按压，每穴1至2分钟。最后用指腹轻拍全头头皮30秒，以进一步激发气血。每天早晚各做一次，每次5至10分钟，坚持一个月以上即可感到头皮出油减少、头发脱落改善。

zh.title: 黑芝麻养发糊
zh.instructions:
1. 黑芝麻、核桃炒香
2. 研磨成粉
3. 加入枸杞
4. 用温水调成糊状
5. 加入蜂蜜调味
6. 每日食用，补肾养发

zh.text: 养发生活习惯

养发之事，三分靠治、七分靠养，生活习惯的调整远比依赖某种特效产品更为重要。规律作息是第一要义——晚上11点至凌晨3点是肝胆经当令之时，此时深度睡眠最有助于肝血修复和肾精保养，"人卧则血归于肝"，熬夜直接耗伤肝肾精血。情绪调节同样不可忽视——肝气郁结会导致头皮气血供应不足，保持心情舒畅对养发至关重要。适度运动如散步、慢跑、太极等可以促进全身气血运行，改善头部供血。饮食上多摄入黑芝麻、黑豆、桑葚、核桃等补肾养血的食物。此外，房事应有节制，过度频繁会耗伤肾精，加速脱发和白发。
护发注意事项

在日常护发中，有些细节同样需要注意。频繁的染烫会直接损伤发质和头皮，化学成分反复刺激会加速脱发。洗发应选用温和的氨基酸类或中药洗发产品，避免强碱性产品刺激头皮。洗头时水温不宜过高，以37至40摄氏度为佳。不要过度用力拉扯头发，湿发时尤其脆弱。保持头皮清洁但不过度清洁——每天洗头反而会破坏头皮屏障，导致油脂分泌紊乱。吹风机温度不宜过高，距离头皮15厘米以上。这些细节虽然看似琐碎，但长期坚持对保护头发健康有着实实在在的帮助。
温馨提示：养发需要长期坚持，不可急于求成。短期内大量脱发或头皮出现明显异常（红斑、鳞屑、瘙痒等）建议及时到皮肤科就诊。严重脱发建议在专业中医师辨证指导下进行综合调理，配合药物治疗效果更佳。

en.text: Hair has always been regarded in TCM as an external indicator of the body's abundance or deficiency of qi and blood. Two foundational passages from the Huang Di Nei Jing established the theoretical basis of TCM hair care: "The kidney stores essence, and its brilliance manifests in the hair," and "The liver stores blood, and hair is the surplus of blood." These statements reveal a core principle — the condition, luster, density, and color of hair reflect the abundance of liver and kidney essence and blood. In my clinical practice, I encounter countless hair loss patients who arrive with expensive topical products, yet few realize that hair problems are alarm signals of internal imbalance. Without addressing the root cause, external applications alone will never achieve satisfactory results.
TCM Understanding of Hair

TCM holds that hair growth depends on the nourishment of essence and blood. The General Treatise on the Etiology and Symptomatology of Diseases states: "The foot shaoyin kidney meridian manifests its brilliance in the hair. The Chong and Ren meridians are the sea of the twelve meridians, known as the blood sea... When qi and blood are abundant, they nourish the hair, making it beautiful; when qi and blood decline and the meridians become depleted, they can no longer moisten the hair, and it falls out." This passage incisively elucidates the necessary connection between hair condition and the fullness of qi and blood. Specifically, kidney essence directly affects hair density and color — abundant kidney essence yields thick, dark hair, while depleted kidney essence leads to sparse, prematurely gray hair. Liver blood affects hair moisture — when liver blood rises to nourish the hair, it is soft and lustrous; when liver blood is deficient, the hair becomes dry and brittle.
Kidney & Hair

The Su Wen describes the entire human life cycle through the waxing and waning of kidney qi, stating: "At age 35 for women, the yangming meridian declines, the face begins to wither, and hair begins to fall... At age 40 for men, kidney qi declines, hair falls and teeth wither." Those with sufficient kidney essence naturally have thick, lustrous hair; those with insufficient kidney essence experience dry, falling, and graying hair. I often use an analogy: kidney essence is like the "savings account" for your hair. If you squander it in youth through chronic sleep deprivation, overexertion, and excessive sexual activity, your hair will be "overdrawn" well before old age. In my clinical practice, patients in their twenties and thirties with severe hair loss and premature graying almost invariably have histories of chronic late nights and high-stress lifestyles.
Liver & Hair

The Lingshu states: "The foot jueyin liver meridian... ascends to the forehead and meets the du meridian at the vertex." The liver stores blood, and the jueyin meridian reaches the top of the head. When liver blood is abundant, the meridian is nourished, the hair roots are secure, and the hair strands are moist. When liver blood is deficient, the hair roots lose nourishment — mild cases present as dryness and split ends, while severe cases lead to thinning and shedding. Furthermore, the liver governs smooth flow of qi. Liver qi stagnation also affects hair health — qi stagnation leads to blood stasis, reducing blood supply to the scalp, and the hair follicles cannot maintain their normal growth cycle. In treating female hair loss patients, I place particular emphasis on soothing the liver and resolving stagnation, as liver depression constitutes a significant proportion of etiological factors in women.
Causes of Hair Problems
Hair Loss Causes

Hair loss can be attributed to four primary pathological states in TCM. The first is kidney essence deficiency — either congenital insufficiency or acquired excessive depletion (from late nights, overwork, or uncontrolled sexual activity), leaving insufficient essence to nourish the hair. The second is qi-blood deficiency — the spleen is the source of qi and blood production, and poor diet or weak spleen function leads to inadequate generation of qi and blood, depriving the hair of nourishment. The third is liver qi stagnation — emotional stress causes liver qi to become constrained, impairing qi and blood circulation and reducing blood supply to the scalp. The fourth is damp-heat ascending — excessive consumption of rich, fatty, and sweet foods generates internal damp-heat, which ascends along the meridians to the scalp, manifesting as an oily scalp, clogged follicles, and seborrheic alopecia. These four causes may appear independently but more frequently intertwine. Careful differentiation of the primary pattern is essential for effective treatment.
White Hair Causes

The appearance of white hair is also closely linked to the liver and kidney. Kidney essence deficiency is the fundamental cause of premature graying — the Su Wen states that when kidney qi declines, "hair and temples turn white." Qi-blood deficiency is another common cause — as hair is the surplus of blood, when qi and blood are insufficient, the hair loses its capacity for pigmentation. Emotional imbalance is equally significant — in my clinical observation, individuals with chronic anxiety and high stress levels develop white hair earlier and more rapidly than the general population. Genetic predisposition also plays an important role — some individuals are born with inherently weaker kidney essence and begin graying in their early thirties. While congenital factors cannot be reversed, their progression can certainly be delayed through proper acquired care.
Hair Care Methods
Tonify Kidney, Nourish Hair

Tonifying the kidney is the foremost priority in hair care, and black-colored foods are the representatives of kidney nourishment. Black sesame, being black in color and entering the kidney meridian, is recorded in the Ben Cao Bei Yao as "tonifying the liver and kidney, moistening the five viscera, and replenishing marrow" — its rich oil content naturally moisturizes the hair. Walnuts, resembling the brain in shape, tonify the kidney and nourish both brain and hair. He Shou Wu (Fleeceflower root) is praised in the Ben Cao Gang Mu as "an excellent tonic that nourishes blood and liver, secures essence and kidney, strengthens bones and sinews, and blackens the beard and hair" — it is one of the most famous TCM herbs for hair care. However, raw He Shou Wu has hepatotoxicity and must be processed before use; long-term high-dose use should also be avoided. Goji berries nourish the liver and kidney and benefit essence and vision — chewed daily or steeped as tea, they produce excellent hair-nourishing effects. Black beans tonify the kidney and benefit essence — they can be cooked as porridge or ground into milk.
Nourish Blood, Care for Hair

Nourishing blood is the other important pillar of hair care. Angelica sinensis is called "the holy herb for blood" in the Ben Cao Gang Mu — it both tonifies and activates blood, generating new blood while moving existing blood, making it the first choice for nourishing blood to care for hair. Prepared rehmannia, after nine rounds of steaming and drying, transforms from cool to warm in nature, greatly enhancing its power to tonify blood and nourish yin — it is often used in combination with angelica. Donkey-hide gelatin, made from donkey hide, tonifies blood and nourishes yin, moistens dryness and stops bleeding — the Ben Cao Gang Mu states it "harmonizes blood and nourishes yin, dispels wind and moistens dryness," making it highly effective for improving dry, brittle hair and hair loss due to blood deficiency. Red dates tonify qi and blood, with gentle but reliable effects suitable for long-term daily dietary therapy. In clinical practice, I frequently combine angelica, prepared rehmannia, and red dates with astragalus (to tonify qi and generate blood) as a tea or soup base for long-term regulation in patients with combined qi and blood deficiency.
Hair Care Acupoints

Scalp acupoint massage is an important method for hair care. Baihui (GV20), at the vertex of the head, is the meeting point of all yang meridians — massaging it raises yang qi, promotes cranial circulation, and stimulates follicle activity. Shenshu (BL23), located 1.5 cun lateral to the lower border of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra, though not on the head, treats hair by tonifying the kidney — a classic application of "treating upper body disorders through lower body points." Taixi (KI3), in the depression between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon, is the source point of the kidney meridian — pressing it tonifies the kidney and benefits essence. Sanyinjiao (SP6), 3 cun above the medial malleolus on the medial leg, is the meeting point of the liver, spleen, and kidney meridians — it notably regulates and tonifies qi and blood. Fengchi (GB20), at the back of the neck, improves cranial blood supply when massaged. I recommend that patients comb or massage their scalp with fingertips from forehead to nape for 5 to 10 minutes daily, focusing on these acupoints. Consistent practice yields clear improvements in hair quality and reduced shedding.
Scalp Massage Methods

Scalp massage is the simplest and most accessible hair care method. Using the pads of the ten fingers, begin at the frontal hairline and make spiral kneading motions along the scalp toward the back of the neck, with moderate pressure until the scalp feels slightly warm. Then use a wooden or horn comb to slowly comb from forehead to nape, 50 to 100 strokes, to effectively promote scalp circulation. Baihui and Fengchi can be specifically pressed with the thumb or index finger for 1 to 2 minutes each. Finally, gently tap the entire scalp with fingertips for 30 seconds to further stimulate qi and blood. Perform this routine morning and evening, 5 to 10 minutes each session. After one month of consistent practice, most patients notice reduced scalp oiliness and decreased hair shedding.

en.title: Black Sesame Hair Nourishing Paste
en.instructions:
1. Toast black sesame and walnut
2. Grind into powder
3. Add goji berries
4. Mix with warm water into paste
5. Add honey to taste
6. Eat daily, tonifies kidney, nourishes hair

en.text: Hair Care Lifestyle Habits

Hair care follows the principle that three parts rely on treatment and seven parts on maintenance — lifestyle adjustments are far more important than relying on any specific miracle product. Regular sleep is the first essential: from 11 PM to 3 AM is the time when the liver and gallbladder meridians are most active. Deep sleep during this period is crucial for liver blood repair and kidney essence preservation — "when a person lies down, blood returns to the liver." Staying up late directly depletes liver and kidney essence and blood. Emotional balance is equally critical — liver qi stagnation reduces blood supply to the scalp, and maintaining a cheerful disposition is vital for hair health. Moderate exercise such as walking, jogging, and tai chi promotes systemic qi and blood circulation, improving cranial blood supply. The diet should emphasize black sesame, black beans, mulberries, and walnuts — foods that tonify the kidney and nourish blood. Additionally, sexual activity should be moderate, as excessive indulgence depletes kidney essence and accelerates both hair loss and graying.
Hair Protection Notes

In daily hair care, certain details deserve attention. Frequent dyeing and perming directly damage hair quality and the scalp — repeated chemical exposure accelerates hair loss. Choose gentle amino acid-based or herbal shampoos, avoiding harsh alkaline products. Shampoo water temperature should not exceed 37 to 40 degrees Celsius. Avoid aggressively pulling or tugging the hair, which is especially fragile when wet. Maintain scalp cleanliness without over-washing — daily washing can damage the scalp barrier and cause sebum secretion dysregulation. When using a hairdryer, keep the temperature moderate and maintain a distance of at least 15 centimeters from the scalp. Although these details may seem trivial, consistent attention to them provides tangible benefits for preserving hair health over the long term.

Note: Hair care requires long-term commitment and patience. Sudden massive hair loss or obvious scalp abnormalities (red spots, scaling, itching) warrant prompt dermatological evaluation. Severe hair loss should be treated comprehensively under the guidance of a qualified TCM practitioner following proper pattern differentiation, with medication for best results.
